key_insight: Closing a differentiable loop between Human Mesh Recovery (HMR) and Gaussian Splatting avatars lets each system supervise and correct the other, producing substantially more accurate 3D human geometry and consistent appearance across views.
problem_solved: Existing pipelines either overfit to 2D cues (ViT-based HMR) or produce appearance-focused but geometrically imprecise avatars (NeRF/Gaussian Splatting), yielding inaccurate 3D human geometry and inconsistent novel-view renderings.
method: Create a closed-loop pipeline where HMR produces an initial mesh, which is converted into a Gaussian Splatting avatar and rendered to generate multi-view supervision.
Backpropagate differences between rendered splat views and input video to update HMR predictions; jointly optimize mesh parameters and Gaussian splat attributes for coherent geometry + appearance.
Iterative refinement: alternate between mesh recovery and splat optimization to converge on accurate 3D shape and photorealistic rendering.
impact: Provides practitioners a practical way to get reliable, view-consistent 3D human avatars from video—improving motion capture, virtual production, and any ML task that needs accurate human geometry or novel-view synthesis.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing the closed loop: video → HMR mesh → Gaussian Splat avatar → rendered views → loss → HMR update
Before vs after geometry comparisons (mesh overlays and point clouds) to highlight geometric correction
Quantitative bar/line chart comparing 3D error and novel-view fidelity against ViT-based and NeRF/Gaussian baselines
Example video frames alongside final rendered avatar novel views (visual fidelity + temporal consistency)
paper_title: HumanSplatHMR: Closing the Loop Between Human Mesh Recovery and Gaussian Splatting Avatar
paper_authors: Yeheng Zong, Pou-Chun Kung, Yike Pan, Seth Isaacson, Yizhou Chen
